newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by foreign trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by foreign trade.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Friday, in trade dominated by foreign buying, brokers said.
The all share index closed 9.0 points higher at 819.7 with highly capitalised blue chips Development Finance rising 10 rupees to 300, and John Keells Holdings 15 rupees to 350.
"Barring unforseen incidents ... we expect the index to head up on good (earnings) growth expectations," said Gordon Nadesan of CT Smith.
Turnover was 84.6 million rupees, led by 90,000 National Development Bank shares and 60,000 Lanka Lubricants.
Analysts expect the market to rise to about 830 points before profit-taking sets in.
"Also, if interest rates remain low, investors will continue to be attracted to the market," said one analyst.
A sum of 622.2 million rupees was also raised in Colombo on Friday through the sale of 51 percent or 10.2 million shares of Malwatte Valley Plantations Ltd, at 61 rupees per share.
The transaction, which went through as an extraordinary item, saw the government sell a strategic holding in a plantation firm. Three more similar deals are due to take place next week.
